title: A bill to provide for the extension of the enforcement instruction on supervision requirements for outpatient therapeutic services in critical access and small rural hospitals through 2015.
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was reported to the Senate on July 30, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

(Sec. 1) This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services to continue to instruct Medicare contractors not to enforce requirements for direct physician supervision of outpatient therapeutic services in critical access and small rural hospitals through 2015.

summary.headline: A 2015 law told Medicare contractors to keep pausing enforcement of a physician supervision rule for certain therapy services at small rural and critical access hospitals through 2015.
summary.what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Health and Human Services to keep telling Medicare contractors not to enforce direct physician supervision requirements for outpatient therapeutic services at critical access and small rural hospitals. The extension covers the period through the end of 2015. The summary describes this as a continuation of an existing instruction rather than a new rule.

who_it_affects.group: Critical access and small rural hospitals
who_it_affects.how: They are not required to meet the direct physician supervision requirement for certain outpatient therapy services through the end of 2015.

who_it_affects.group: Medicare patients using outpatient therapy at these hospitals
who_it_affects.how: Their covered therapy services at these facilities continued under the enforcement pause during 2015.
They were directed to continue not enforcing the direct physician supervision requirement for these services through 2015.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 18, 2015, and applies through the end of 2015.
